title: Olney: Red Sox have expressed interest in Marlins All-Star Otto Lopez
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox show interest in Miami Marlins All-Star shortstop Otto Lopez, who leads MLB with a .331 batting average.
Boston's search for a shortstop is urgent, worsened by Curtis Mead's injury and Trevor Story's ongoing recovery.
Lopez, 27, shines with 27 doubles, nine home runs, and 48 RBI, and is under team control through 2030.

title: New Red Sox Curtis Mead lands on IL with broken wrist after 1 game with Boston
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Curtis Mead placed on injured list with a fractured wrist after debut with Red Sox against Athletics.
Mead injured by a 95 mph pitch from Jack Perkins; initial X-rays were negative, later tests revealed fracture.
Nick Sogard called up from Triple-A Worcester to replace Mead; Red Sox might seek additional offense by trade deadline.

title: Watertown police shut down 4 bodyworks establishments after inspections
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Watertown police closed four bodyworks establishments for licensing and occupancy violations after city inspections.
Thai Body Spa was shut down for lacking permits and possessing items of a sexual nature, police reported.
Authorities will allow businesses to reopen after compliance with city rules and an additional inspection.

title: Boston Shriners Hospital says it’s seeing multiple burn patients every week from this popular type of toy
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Shriners Children's Boston reports multiple severe burn cases from gel-filled fidget toys exploding, especially during summer.
A social media trend of microwaving these toys causes scald and chemical burns from overheated gel rupturing the silicone shell.
Doctors warn about burn risks from knockoff toys; body heat, outdoor heat, or freezing can also cause ruptures.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 4 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Kayshon Boutte is proving essential to the Patriots, showcasing key plays amid trade rumors during training camp.
Injuries impacted the Patriots' cornerback depth, with Carlton Davis and Charles Woods leaving Tuesday's practice.
Rookie Caleb Lomu is performing well in training camp, competing in 1-on-1 battles and earning tackle reps.

title: After local pushback, popular wildlife clinic moves on from ‘perfect’ Carlisle property
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Newhouse Wildlife Rescue abandons plans for Carlisle property after local pushback regarding safety and traffic concerns.
The Chelmsford-based wildlife clinic sought the Carlisle property for its 13.1-acre space, ideal for animal rehabilitation.
Despite securing a Dover Amendment determination, the clinic faced opposition from abutters worried about increased traffic.

title: Patriots’ WR Kyle Williams is staying upbeat despite limited training camp snaps
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Kyle Williams aims to capitalize on limited opportunities during Patriots training camp amid strong receiver competition.
Williams, entering his second NFL season, emphasizes controlling what he can and improving his physicality.
Coach Mike Vrabel praised Williams for offseason efforts; Williams also a potential candidate for kick returner role.

title: Boston is about to lose its last Boloco
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boloco will close its last Boston location at 50 Congress St. on September 25 due to a building conversion.
The closure marks the end of Boloco's nearly 30-year presence, once boasting 22 locations across New England.
Boloco was founded in 1997 and saw ownership changes, ending with co-founder John Pepper's leadership since 2015.

title: Online and phone lottery games are now live in Mass. Here’s what to know.
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Mass Lottery Online launches, enabling players 21+ to gamble from phones, tablets, or computers with Mega Millions, Powerball, and eInstant games.
Keno remains retail-only, while online games can be played on one device per account with multi-factor authentication for security.
Online lottery winnings under $601 are automatically deposited, while larger prizes require claims; profits support early childhood education grants.

title: These celebrities will all be in Boston next weekend
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: Fan Expo Boston 2026 will feature celebrities like Chris Evans, Mel Gibson, and Elijah Wood at the Menino Convention & Exhibition Center.
The event includes panels, autograph sessions, cosplay contests, and more, running from August 7-9 with daily general admission tickets from $45.
Highlights include a 'Lord of the Rings' 25th anniversary panel and a Captain America discussion with Chris Evans on August 9.
